title: Pavement Markers and Traffic Lines, Typical Details (Centerlines, Lane Lines and No Passing Zones)
summary: Caltrans 2026 Standard Plan A20A gives typical plan-view patterns for 6 in. yellow and white traffic lines with Type C, D, G and H retroreflective pavement markers. It covers two-lane highway centerlines (Details 1 to 7), multilane lane lines (Details 8 to 14A) and no passing zone lines in one and two directions (Details 15 to 23). Details 3, 4, 7, 10, 13, 14, 14A, 17, 20 and 23 are deleted.
description:
Overall layout: Sheet 14 of the 2026 Standard Plan set, no scale. Every pattern is drawn in plan with arrows showing the direction of travel and dimension strings giving the repeating cycle. Line patterns use a hatched box for a 6 in. yellow line and an open box for a 6 in. white line. Markers are small squares: Type C red-clear (square with vertical and horizontal split), Type D two-way yellow (square with X), Type G one-way clear (half filled black) and Type H one-way yellow (half black with X hatch). Right side of the sheet also shows the marker detail drawings and a note.

Centerlines (2 lane highways), Detail 1: Two opposing arrows. Broken 6 in. yellow line with 7'-0" painted segments and 17'-0" gaps (24'-0" cycle). No markers shown.

Detail 2: Same 7'-0" segment and 17'-0" gap broken yellow line, dimensioned over a 48'-0" length, with a Type D marker placed 8'-6" before the first segment and 8'-6" after the last segment, so the dimensions add to 48'-0" (8'-6" + 7'-0" + 17'-0" + 7'-0" + 8'-6").

Detail 3: Deleted. Detail 4: Deleted.

Detail 5: Broken 6 in. yellow line with a 12'-0" segment and a 36'-0" gap (48'-0" cycle). No markers shown.

Detail 6: Broken yellow line on a 48'-0" cycle: 18'-0" gap, 12'-0" segment, 18'-0" gap, with a Type D marker at the 48'-0" cycle point.

Detail 7: Deleted.

Lane lines (multilane highways), Detail 8: Two same-direction arrows. Broken 6 in. white line with 7'-0" segments and 17'-0" gaps (24'-0" cycle). No markers.

Detail 9: Broken white line, 48'-0" dimension: 8'-6" to the first segment, 7'-0" segment, 17'-0" gap, 7'-0" segment, 8'-6" after. A Type G one-way clear marker at the start of the 48'-0" dimension, 8'-6" ahead of the first segment.

Detail 9A: Same geometry as Detail 9 (8'-6", 7'-0", 17'-0", 7'-0", 8'-6" over 48'-0") but the marker is a Type C red-clear marker.

Detail 10: Deleted.

Detail 11: Broken 6 in. white line with a 12'-0" segment and a 36'-0" gap (48'-0" cycle). No markers.

Detail 12: Broken white line on a 48'-0" cycle: 18'-0" gap, 12'-0" segment, 18'-0" gap, with a Type G marker at the cycle point.

Detail 12A: Same as Detail 12 (18'-0", 12'-0", 18'-0" over 48'-0") with a Type C red-clear marker.

Details 13, 14 and 14A: Deleted.

Marker details (top center and right): Type C and Type D marker: plan about 3 7/8 in. to 4 1/2 in. wide by 1 7/8 in. to 4 1/8 in. tall (as drawn: width 3 7/8"-4 1/2", height 1 7/8"-4 1/8"), side profile height 3/8 in. to 3/4 in. (3/8"-3/4"), with the retroreflective face hatched on both the top and bottom ends of the plan view (two-way face). Type G and Type H marker: same overall dimensions, with a black non-reflective body on one side and the retroreflective face on the other (one-way face).

No passing zones, one direction, Detail 15: Opposing arrows with a dash-dot reference line labeled LOL between them. A continuous 6 in. yellow solid line along the LOL on the no passing side, and a broken yellow line on the other side with 7'-0" segments and 17'-0" gaps (24'-0" cycle). Offset dimensions at the right end show 3 in. and 1 1/2 in. between the line edges and the LOL. No markers.

Detail 16: Solid yellow line plus a broken yellow line with 8'-6", 7'-0", 8'-6" over a 48'-0" dimension. Type D markers placed 8'-6" before and after the broken segment on the broken line side, and Type H markers on the solid line side at 24'-0" spacing. A 2 in. dimension at the right end shows marker offset from the solid line, with 3 in. and 1 1/2 in. dimensions to the LOL.

Detail 17: Deleted.

Detail 18: Solid yellow line plus a broken yellow line with a 12'-0" segment and 36'-0" gap. Dimensions at the right: 3 in. and 1 1/2 in. No markers.

Detail 19: Solid yellow line plus a broken yellow line with 18'-0" gap, 12'-0" segment and 18'-0" gap. Type D markers on the broken line side at the cycle points and Type H markers on the solid line side at 24'-0" spacing. 2 in., 3 in. and 1 1/2 in. dimensions at the right end.

Detail 20: Deleted.

No passing zones, two direction, Detail 21: Two parallel solid 6 in. yellow lines with LOL between them and 3 in. and 1 1/2 in. dimensions at the right end. No markers.

Detail 22: Two parallel solid yellow lines with LOL between them. Type D markers on both outer sides at 24'-0" spacing. 2 in., 3 in. and 1 1/2 in. dimensions at the right end.

Detail 23: Deleted.

Legend: Type C red-clear retroreflective marker, Type D two-way yellow retroreflective marker, Type G one-way clear retroreflective marker, Type H one-way yellow retroreflective marker, 6 in. white line, 6 in. yellow line.
notes:
Note: Pavement markers shown off the solid line may be placed on the line.

Legend:
Type C red-clear retroreflective marker.
Type D two-way yellow retroreflective marker.
Type G one-way clear retroreflective marker.
Type H one-way yellow retroreflective marker.

title: Pavement Markers and Traffic Lines, Typical Details (Edge Lines, Median Islands, Two-Way Left Turn Lanes, Intersection Treatments)
summary: Caltrans 2026 Standard Plan A20B gives plan-view patterns for left and right edge lines, median island double yellow lines, two-way left turn lane lines and the approach to an intersecting street centerline, with Type D, H and RY markers. Details 24 to 27C, 28, 29, 31, 32, 34, 34A, 35 and 35A are active. Details 27A, 30 and 33 are deleted.
description:
Overall layout: Sheet 15 of the 2026 Standard Plan set, no scale. Patterns are drawn in plan with arrows for the direction of travel. ETW labels a dashed reference line that is the edge of traveled way, and LOL labels a dash-dot reference line between the paired lines in median and left turn lane details. Hatched boxes are 6 in. yellow lines and open boxes are 6 in. white lines. Marker symbols are Type D two-way yellow (square with X), Type H one-way yellow (half black) and Type RY red-yellow (square with cross lines).

Left edge lines (divided highways), Detail 24: A continuous 6 in. yellow line on the left edge, placed 2 in. from the ETW reference line (2 in. dimension at right end). No markers.

Detail 25: Same continuous yellow line with Type H markers on the line side 2 in. from the line (2 in. dimensions at both ends), spaced 48'-0" apart.

Detail 25A: Same yellow line with Type RY markers at 24'-0" spacing (two 24'-0" dimensions shown between three markers, with a marker at each end of the 48'-0" length).

Detail 25B: Same yellow line with Type RY markers at 48'-0" spacing.

Detail 26: No solid line. A broken reference at the ETW with Type H markers 48'-0" apart and a 2 in. offset dimension at the right end.

Detail 26A: As Detail 26 with Type RY markers 48'-0" apart.

Detail 26B: Two parallel continuous yellow lines (3 in. between them, 2 in. offset from the ETW at the left and right ends) with Type RY markers 48'-0" apart.

Detail 27: As Detail 26B (two continuous yellow lines, 3 in. spacing, 2 in. offset) with Type H markers 48'-0" apart.

Left edge lines note (bottom left): On freeways use traffic stripe details with Type RY markers.

Right edge lines, Detail 27A: Deleted.

Detail 27B: A continuous 6 in. white right edge line with a 2 in. offset dimension from the ETW reference line. No markers.

Right edge line extension through intersections, Detail 27C: Short 6 in. white line segments, each 3'-0" long, separated by 12'-0" gaps (dimensioned 12'-0" between segments and 3'-0" along each segment).

Median islands, Detail 28: Two pairs of continuous yellow lines on either side of the LOL line. The nearest line of each pair is 2'-0" minimum from the LOL line. Each pair has 3 in. spacing between the lines (3 in. dimension at right end). No markers.

Detail 29: Same as Detail 28 (2'-0" Min from LOL, 3 in. between lines) with Type D markers outside each pair at 24'-0" spacing, with a 2 in. offset dimension at the right end.

Detail 30: Deleted.

Two-way left turn lanes, Detail 31: Two outer continuous yellow lines with a broken yellow line inside each, arranged symmetrically about the LOL line. Broken segments are 12'-0" long with 36'-0" gaps. The broken line is 3 in. and 1 1/2 in. from the solid line, and the two broken lines are 12'-0" Typ apart (as drawn at the right end). No markers.

Detail 32: Same arrangement with Type D markers. Markers are spaced 24'-0" along the outside of each solid line, dimensioned over a 96'-0" length. The broken lines, from the 96'-0" dimension start, show 18'-0" gap, 12'-0" segment, 36'-0" gap, 12'-0" segment, 36'-0" gap. Type D markers also appear inside the lane between broken segments. 2 in. offset dimensions on the outer markers and 3 in. and 1 1/2 in. dimensions at the right end.

Detail 33: Deleted.

Intersection treatments, Detail 34: Continuous yellow line along the approach and a broken yellow line, each ending at the centerline of the intersecting street with a break symbol and "100'-0" Min" dimension from the intersection. Broken segments are 12'-0" with gaps of 18'-0", 18'-0", 12'-0" and 18'-0" (as dimensioned above the line). Type D markers sit on the broken line side and Type H markers on the solid line side at 24'-0" spacing. Dimensions at left end: 1 1/2 in., 3 in. and 2 in. Pattern repeats mirrored on the far side of the intersecting street.

Detail 34A: Continuous yellow line with a broken yellow line of 12'-0" segment, 36'-0" gap, 12'-0" segment, over a 100'-0" Min length to the intersecting street centerline. 3 in. and 1 1/2 in. dimensions. No markers.

Detail 35: Continuous yellow line with a broken line of 7'-0" segments and gaps dimensioned 8'-6", 8'-6", 7'-0", 8'-6", over a 100'-0" Min length. Type H markers on the solid line side and Type D markers on the broken side at 24'-0" spacing. 3 in., 1 1/2 in. and 2 in. dimensions.

Detail 35A: Continuous yellow line with a broken line of 7'-0" segments and 17'-0" gaps (shown 17'-0" and 7'-0" at the intersection end) over a 100'-0" Min length. 1 1/2 in. and 3 in. dimensions. No markers.

The right half of the intersection treatment panel (beyond the line labeled CENTERLINE INTERSECTING STREET) repeats Details 34, 34A, 35 and 35A for the opposite approach with the same dimensions: 24'-0" marker spacing, 18'-0" and 12'-0" gaps, 12'-0" and 36'-0" cycle, 8'-6" and 7'-0" segments, 17'-0" and 7'-0" cycle, 100'-0" Min, and 2 in., 3 in. and 1 1/2 in. offsets, with an LOL line.

Marker details (right): Type RY and Type D marker: plan about 3 7/8 in. to 4 1/2 in. wide by 1 7/8 in. to 4 1/8 in. tall, side profile 3/8 in. to 3/4 in., retroreflective face hatched on both ends. Type H marker: same dimensions with a black body on one end and a one-way retroreflective face.

Legend: Type D two-way yellow retroreflective marker, Type H one-way yellow retroreflective marker, Type RY red-yellow retroreflective marker, 6 in. white line, 6 in. yellow line.
notes:
Note: Pavement markers shown off the solid line may be placed on the line.

Left edge lines note: On freeways use traffic stripe details with Type RY markers.

Legend:

Type H one-way yellow retroreflective marker.
Type RY red-yellow retroreflective marker.

title: Pavement Markers and Traffic Lines, Typical Details (Ramp Gore Treatments, Lane Drops and Chevron Markings)
summary: Caltrans 2026 Standard Plan A20C shows ramp neutral area and gore striping for exit ramps, entrance ramp merges and acceleration lanes (Details 36, 36A, 36B), 8 in. white lane drop patterns at exit ramps and intersections (Details 37 and 37B), and 45 degree chevron markings for exit and entrance gores. Details 37A and 37C are deleted.
description:
Overall layout: Sheet 16 of the 2026 Standard Plan set, no scale. Plan views of ramp gores read left to right with arrows showing the direction of travel. Marker symbols: Type C red-clear (square with cross lines), Type G one-way clear (half black) and Type RY red-yellow (hatched square).

Exit ramp neutral area (gore) treatment, Detail 36: Mainline edge of traveled way (top) is a broken white line with Type C markers every 24'-0" and a 2 in. offset. Below it, a 12 in. white line runs along the mainline side of the gore, 1'-0" below the edge line, to the theoretical gore point, then a 12 in. white line diverges along the ramp edge. The ramp edge of traveled way carries a broken line with Type C markers every 24'-0" and a 2 in. offset. Past a break symbol the 6 in. white line reaches the physical gore (see Detail 27B, Standard Plan A20B) and a 6 in. yellow line runs along the ramp side of the physical gore (see Detail 25A, Standard Plan A20B). Chevron marking is called out (see chevron marking detail).

Entrance ramp neutral area (merge) treatment, Detail 36A: Mainline edge line with a 6 in. white line (see Detail 27B, Standard Plan A20B) at the physical gore, a 12 in. white line along the mainline and ramp sides of the gore, 6'-0" dimension between the ramp edge and mainline edge at the merge, 24'-0" marker spacing and 2 in. offset on the ramp edge with Type C markers, and a 6 in. yellow line at the physical gore (see Detail 25A, Standard Plan A20B). Downstream segments of the ramp and mainline edge lines use Detail 8 or 9A, Standard Plan A20A.

Entrance ramp neutral area (acceleration lane) treatment, Detail 36B: Similar to Detail 36A with the 12 in. white line continuing along the acceleration lane to the theoretical gore point, a 6 in. white line (Detail 27B, Standard Plan A20B), a 6 in. yellow line at the physical gore (Detail 25A, Standard Plan A20B), Type C markers at 24'-0" with a 2 in. offset on the ramp edge, and mainline edge of traveled way as a broken line.

Lane drop at exit ramps, Detail 37: Broken 8 in. white line with Type C markers placed every 30'-0" (two 30'-0" dimensions shown). Dimensions locate each marker and segment: 6'-0", 12'-0", 6'-0" and 3'-0" in each cycle. At the right end, a 300'-0" dimension (note *) leads to the exit ramp where the pattern joins Detail 36 and the solid channelizing line of Detail 38B, Standard Plan A20D, with 3'-0" and 6'-0" dimensions at the start of the line.

Detail 37A: Deleted.

Lane drop at intersections, Detail 37B: Same 8 in. white broken line with Type G markers every 30'-0", 6'-0", 12'-0", 6'-0" and 3'-0" dimensions, ending in the solid 8 in. white channelizing line (Detail 38B, Standard Plan A20D) at the intersection. Direction of through traffic is shown.

Detail 37C: Deleted.

Chevron pavement markings at exit ramp gore area: 12 in. white chevron lines at 45 degrees to the gore edge lines, 18 in. between chevron legs, chevrons 50'-0" apart, first chevron at 6'-0" dimension from the mainline side. The gore is bounded by 12 in. white lines on the ramp side (see Detail 36).

Chevron pavement markings at entrance ramp gore area: The same 45 degree chevrons, 18 in. leg spacing and 50'-0" spacing, bounded by 12 in. white lines (see Details 36A or 36B).

Marker details: Type C and Type RY marker plan about 3 7/8 in. to 4 1/2 in. wide and 1 7/8 in. to 4 1/8 in. tall, side profile 3/8 in. to 3/4 in. high, retroreflective face on both ends. Type G marker same dimensions with a black body on one end.

Legend: Type RY red-yellow retroreflective marker, Type G one-way clear retroreflective marker, Type C red-clear retroreflective marker.
notes:
1. Install a minimum of 1 chevron in the gore area. If at least 1 chevron will not fit into the gore area, do not install chevrons.

2. Terminate chevron markings at physical gore.

3. Gore area chevron pavement markings shown. For exit and entrance ramp channelizing lines details, see Details 36, 36A, and 36B.

* The solid channelizing line shown may be omitted on short auxiliary lanes where weaving length is critical.

Legend:
Type RY red-yellow retroreflective marker.
Type G one-way clear retroreflective marker.
Type C red-clear retroreflective marker.

Details 37A and 37C are marked deleted. Return to Table of Contents link at the bottom of the page.

title: Pavement Markers and Traffic Lines, Typical Details (Channelizing, Bike Lane, Extensions and Recessed Markers)
summary: Caltrans 2026 Standard Plan A20D covers 8 in. white channelizing lines (Details 38 to 38D), 6 in. bike lane lines (39, 39A), lane line and centerline extensions through intersections (40, 41), and recess details for traffic stripes and retroreflective pavement markers. Details 38C, 40A and 41A are deleted.
description:
Overall layout: Sheet 17 of the 2026 Standard Plan set, no scale. The left side shows line patterns in plan, the middle shows marker details and the recessed traffic stripe, and the right shows the recess detail for retroreflective pavement markers. Markers: Type C red-clear (cross-line square) and Type G one-way clear (half black).

Channelizing line, Detail 38: A continuous 8 in. white line with a break symbol at the left end and Type G markers 2 in. below the line at 24'-0" spacing. Through traffic arrow shown.

Detail 38A: Continuous 8 in. white line, no markers.

Detail 38B: Continuous 8 in. white line with Type C markers on both sides at 24'-0" spacing, each 2 in. from the line.

Detail 38C: Deleted.

Detail 38D (exit ramps only): Continuous 8 in. white line with Type C markers on one side at 24'-0" spacing, 2 in. from the line.

Bike lane line, Detail 39: Continuous 6 in. white line.

Intersection line, bike lane, Detail 39A: Broken 6 in. white line of 8'-0" segments with 4'-0" gaps over a 200'-0" length toward the intersection.

Lane line extensions through intersections, Detail 40: Short 6 in. white segments 1'-0" long with 6'-0" gaps.

Detail 40A: Deleted.

Centerline extensions through intersections, Detail 41: Short 6 in. yellow segments 1'-0" long with 6'-0" gaps.

Detail 41A: Deleted.

Marker details: Type C marker plan about 3 7/8 in. to 4 1/2 in. wide and 1 7/8 in. to 4 1/8 in. tall, side profile 3/8 in. to 3/4 in. high, with retroreflective face top and bottom. Type G marker same dimensions with a black body at one end.

Detail for recessed traffic stripe: Section through finished roadway surface showing a recess 6 in. to 8 in. wide filled with striping material flush with the surface (see Recessed Notes A and B).

Recess detail for retroreflective pavement marker, Plan Type 1 and Section A-A: Recess 5 3/16 in. plus or minus 1/8 in. wide, length at least 2'-0" ramp plus 1'-0" min, with the retroreflective pavement marker at the downstream end of the recess. The marker top sits 0 in. to 3/16 in. below the pavement surface (see Note 3). Recess depth varies (Var). See Note 5. Arrow shows direction of traffic.

Plan Type 2 and Section B-B: Same 5 3/16 in. plus or minus 1/8 in. wide recess, 2'-0" Min ramp each side of a 1'-0" Min center section that is 6 in. wide, with the marker at the center of the recess, 0 in. to 3/16 in. below pavement surface, depth Var.

Retroreflective pavement marker for recessed installation, Type C, Type RY and Type D: plan 4 9/16 in. to 4 13/16 in. wide by 2 in. to 2 1/2 in. tall, height 3/8 in. to 7/16 in., two-way retroreflective face. Type G, Type R and Type H: same dimensions with a black end and one-way face. See Notes 1 and 2.

Legend: Type C red-clear retroreflective marker, Type G one-way clear retroreflective marker, 6 in. yellow line.
notes:
Note: Pavement markers shown off the solid line may be placed on the line.

Recessed notes:
A. See typical traffic line details for pavement marking patterns.
B. See Standard Specifications for recess depth and recess striping material thickness.

Recessed marker notes:
1. See typical traffic line details for marker patterns to be used with recessed pavement markers.
2. The retroreflective pavement markers shown for recessed installations are not to be used for non-recessed installations.
3. The top of pavement markers installed in recesses shall be 0 in. to 3/16 in. below the pavement surface.
4. Use Type 1 recess for pavement markers with one-way retroreflective face. Use Type 2 recess for pavement markers with two-way retroreflective face.
5. For exit ramps, use Type 1 recess for Type R markers with one-way retroreflective face. Reverse the orientation of the recess and place the marker at the upstream end of the recess.

Legend:
Type C red-clear retroreflective marker.
Type G one-way clear retroreflective marker.
6 in. yellow line.

Details 38C, 40A and 41A are marked deleted. Return to Table of Contents link at the bottom of the page.

title: Traffic Lines, Typical Details for Contrast Striping
summary: Caltrans 2026 Standard Plan A20E shows contrast striping, where black stripes are placed beside or between yellow or white traffic lines to improve visibility on light pavement. It gives a double stripe detail, a lane or edge line detail with 2 in. black borders (Option 1) and a lane line detail with black segments alternating with white segments and a retroreflective marker (Option 2).
description:
Overall layout: Sheet 18 of the 2026 Standard Plan set, no scale. Three plan views of stripes drawn with solid fills: black stripes are filled black, yellow or white lines are drawn as open boxes.

Typical double stripe contrast detail: Three stacked stripes. A yellow or white stripe on top, a black stripe in the middle and a yellow or white stripe on the bottom. The black stripe separates the two colored stripes. No dimensions are given on this view.

Option 1, typical lane line or edge line contrast detail: A yellow or white line (6 in. to 12 in. wide, as dimensioned) between two black stripes. Each black stripe is 2 in. wide and sits directly against the colored line. Dimensions at the right end: 2 in. black, 6 in. to 12 in. colored line, 2 in. black.

Option 2, typical lane line contrast detail (see Note 2): A longitudinal sequence along the lane line. Black segment, then 1'-0" minimum clear space, then a retroreflective marker (half white, half black symbol), then 1'-0" minimum clear space, then a black segment, then a gap of 0' to 2'-0", then a white 6 in. wide segment, then a gap of 0' to 2'-0", then a black segment, and so on. The 6 in. dimension marks the width of the white line. An additional gap of 0' to 2'-0" is shown between the white segment and the next black segment at the left end (white followed by black).
notes:
1. See Standard Plans A20A, A20B, A20C, A20D, and A20F for traffic lines typical details.

2. Detail 9 traffic stripe shown. See project plans for traffic stripe details.

Option labels: Option 1 typical lane line or edge line contrast detail. Option 2 typical lane line contrast detail. Return to Table of Contents link at the bottom of the page.

title: Pavement Markers and Traffic Lines, Typical Details (Preferential Lane Lines)
summary: Caltrans 2026 Standard Plan A20F gives 8 in. white line patterns for preferential lane lines such as HOV and managed lanes. Detail 42 is a broken line with Type C markers, Details 44A, 44B and 45 are double lines with Type C markers and varying buffer space, and Details 43 and 43A are deleted.
description:
Overall layout: Sheet 19 of the 2026 Standard Plan set, no scale. All lines shown are 8 in. white and all markers are Type C red-clear retroreflective markers.

Preferential lane lines, Detail 42: Broken 8 in. white line with 12'-0" segments, an 18'-0" gap, a Type C marker, another 18'-0" gap, and the next 12'-0" segment (48'-0" cycle with the marker at the center of the 36'-0" gap).

Detail 43: Deleted. Detail 43A: Deleted.

Detail 44A: Double solid 8 in. white lines on either side of the LOL line, with a 4 in. space between them (2 in. each side of LOL). Type C markers outside each line 2 in. from the line at 24'-0" spacing. Dimensions at the right end: 2 in. marker offsets and 4 in. space between lines.

Detail 44B: Double solid 8 in. white lines with an 8 in. space between them (4 in. each side of LOL). Type C markers outside each line, 2 in. from it, at 24'-0" spacing. Right end: 8 in. between lines and 2'-0" overall buffer space.

Detail 45: Two pairs of solid 8 in. white lines, one pair on each side of the LOL line. Within each pair the lines are 3 in. apart. Between the two pairs the space is 1 in. to 2 in. on each side of LOL. Type C markers outside each pair, 2 in. from the outer line, at 24'-0" spacing, and a Type C marker on the LOL line (shown as a larger two-cell marker) at 24'-0" spacing. Right end: 3 in. spaces and the overall BUFFER SPACE marked with an asterisk.

title: Exit Ramp with Enhanced Pavement Markers for Wrong Way Details
summary: Caltrans 2026 Standard Plan A20G shows a freeway exit ramp approaching a cross street with enhanced retroreflective pavement markers to discourage wrong-way entry. Type RY markers line the left edge, Type R one-way red markers line the right edge facing wrong-way drivers, Type C markers sit on the lane line, and Type R markers are placed on the outermost limit line or crosswalk. Marker spacing changes in zones of 120 ft, 240 ft and 120 ft ahead of the cross street.
description:
Overall layout: Sheet 20 of the 2026 Standard Plan set, no scale. One plan view of an exit ramp running left to right toward a cross street at the right. Traffic arrows show the ramp direction. Break symbols interrupt the ramp. Dimension strings above and below the ramp measure distances back from the limit line at the cross street. The left edge of the ramp carries a hatched 6 in. yellow edge line and the right edge an edge line, both marked as edge of traveled way. A broken 6 in. white lane line runs down the middle.

Marker details: Type C and Type RY marker plan about 3 7/8 in. to 4 1/2 in. wide by 1 7/8 in. to 4 1/8 in. tall, side profile 3/8 in. to 3/4 in. high, with retroreflective face at both ends. Type R marker same size with a white body (Note 7), one end retroreflective red and the other end non-reflective (black symbol).

Left (top) edge of ramp: Type RY two-way red-yellow markers inboard of the yellow line. Right (bottom) edge: Type R one-way red markers (half black) about 2 in. from the edge of traveled way (2 in. dimension shown near the cross street). Center lane line: white broken segments between Type C red-clear markers spaced 24'-0".

Marker spacing zones (measured upstream from the cross street): The dimensioned zones are 120'-0", 240'-0" and 120'-0" with break symbols. Near the cross street, markers are at 24'-0" spacing (two 24'-0" dimensions at the limit line). Upstream of that the spacing is 12'-0" (two 12'-0" dimensions). In the other zones, clusters of markers at 6'-0" spacing are shown on both edges (6'-0" dimensions) and markers continue at wider spacing between clusters.

Start of ramp (left): Two Type V arrows with Type R one-way red markers beside them, called out See Note 6.

Cross street (right): A limit line or crosswalk (see Note 1) crosses the ramp at the cross street. Three Type R marker groups, drawn as angled V symbols, are placed at the limit line facing the intersection with red facing the intersection (see Notes 1, 2, 3 and 5). The cross street runs vertically, labeled CROSS STREET, with two-way arrows on each approach.

Legend: Type C two-way red-clear retroreflective marker, Type RY two-way red-yellow retroreflective marker, Type R one-way red retroreflective marker, 6 in. white line, 6 in. yellow line.
notes:
1. May be a limit line or crosswalk.

2. See Standard Plans A24F and A24G for crosswalk and pavement marker details.

3. For raised markers, place Type R one-way red retroreflective markers on outermost limit line or crosswalk line with red facing the intersection. For recessed markers, place Type R one-way retroreflective markers with red facing the intersection and as shown on Standard Plan A24G.

4. The distances and marker spacings may be adjusted based on site specific conditions, exit ramp geometry, or loop detectors.

5. See Standard Plan A20D for recess details.

6. See Standard Plan A24G for Type V arrow detail with Type R one-way red retroreflective markers.

7. The Type R marker body must be white in color.

Legend (markers):
Type C two-way red-clear retroreflective marker.
Type RY two-way red-yellow retroreflective marker.
Type R one-way red retroreflective marker.
6 in. white line.
6 in. yellow line.

title: Pavement Markings, Arrows
summary: Caltrans 2026 Standard Plan A24A gives dimensioned grid drawings of nine pavement arrows: Type I in 10, 18 and 24 ft lengths, the bike lane arrow, and Types IV (L), V, VI, VII (L) and VIII. Each is drawn on a grid with its overall width and length and its area in square feet.
description:
Overall layout: Sheet 21 of the 2026 Standard Plan set, no scale. Each arrow is drawn on a grid (1'-0" grid for road arrows and 6 in. grid for the bike lane arrow) with overall dimensions and the area A in square feet shown under the arrow name.

Type I 10'-0" arrow: 3'-6" wide by 10'-0" long, shaft 1'-0" wide (1'-0" dimension at the base), 1'-0" grid, A=14 sq ft.

Type I 18'-0" arrow: 3'-6" wide by 18'-0" long, shaft 1'-0" wide, 1'-0" grid, A=25 sq ft.

Type I 24'-0" arrow: 3'-6" wide by 24'-0" long, shaft 1'-0" wide, 1'-0" grid, A=31 sq ft.

Bike lane arrow: 1'-9" wide by 5'-0" long, shaft 6 in. wide, 6 in. grid, A=3.5 sq ft.

Type IV (L) arrow: left turn arrow with a curved shaft turning left, 6'-0" wide by 8'-0" long, shaft 1'-0" wide, 1'-0" grid, A=15 sq ft. For a Type IV (R) arrow, use mirror image.

Type VI arrow: right lane drop arrow, 5'-6" wide by 18'-0" long (arrowhead length 8'-6", with a 2'-0" dimension at the barb), shaft slanted at 20 degrees to the edge of pavement (labeled EDGE OF PAVEMENT and DIRECTION OF VIEW), 1'-0" grid, A=42 sq ft. For a left lane, use mirror image.

Type V arrow: 24'-0" overall length with a 1'-0" wide stem of 17'-6" length, and two diverging 1'-0" wide legs each 9'-0" long forming a V, with a 2'-0" dimension across the stem and legs, A=33 sq ft.

Type VII (L) arrow: combined through and left turn arrow, 7'-3" wide by 13'-0" long, shaft 1'-0" wide, 1'-0" grid, A=27 sq ft. For a Type VII (R) arrow, use mirror image.

Type VIII arrow: combined left, through and right arrow, 9'-0" wide by 15'-0" long, stem 1'-0" wide with a dashed center line, 1'-0" grid, A=36 sq ft.
notes:
1. Minor variations in dimensions may be accepted by the Engineer.

Arrow notes on the sheet: For Type IV (R) arrow, use mirror image. For Type VI arrow (right lane drop arrow), for left lane use mirror image. For Type VII (R) arrow, use mirror image. A = area in square feet. Return to Table of Contents link at the bottom of the page.

title: Pavement Markings, Arrows and Symbols
summary: Caltrans 2026 Standard Plan A24B gives dimensioned grid drawings of the railroad crossing symbol and the Type II and Type III arrows in left (L) and both-direction (B) versions. Each shows its overall size and area in square feet on a 1 ft grid.
description:
Overall layout: Sheet 22 of the 2026 Standard Plan set, no scale. Each marking is drawn on a 1'-0" grid with overall dimensions and area A in square feet. Dashed lines inside the turn arrows show where the curved shafts merge into the stem.

Railroad crossing symbol: An X with two R letters, centered on the lane. The X is 8'-0" wide by 20'-0" tall, with legs 1'-4" wide. Each R is 6'-0" tall and sits to the left and right of the X crossing point. A transverse line 2'-0" wide by the width of the lane is placed above and below the symbol, each 14'-0" from the X (14'-0" dimensions with break symbols). Area A=70 sq ft. Footnote: 70 SQFT does not include the 2'-0" x variable width transverse lines.

Type II (B) arrow: Straight-through arrow with a left and a right turn branch, 10'-0" wide by 24'-0" long, 1'-0" wide stem, A=59 sq ft.

Type II (L) arrow: Straight-through arrow with a left turn branch, 7'-0" wide by 24'-0" long, 1'-0" wide stem, A=45 sq ft. For Type II (R) use mirror image.

Type III (B) arrow: Left and right turn arrow (no through head) with both curved branches, 11'-0" wide by 24'-0" long, 1'-0" wide stem, A=73 sq ft.

Type III (L) arrow: Left turn arrow with a curved shaft, 6'-0" wide by 24'-0" long, 1'-0" wide stem, A=42 sq ft. For Type III (R) use mirror image.
notes:
1. Minor variations in dimensions may be accepted by the Engineer.

* 70 SQFT does not include the 2'-0" x variable width transverse lines.

For Type II (R) use mirror image. For Type III (R) use mirror image. Return to Table of Contents link at the bottom of the page.

title: Pavement Markings, Symbols and Numerals
summary: Caltrans 2026 Standard Plan A24C gives dimensioned grid drawings of bike lane symbols with and without a rider, the International Symbol of Accessibility marking, the diamond symbol, numerals 25, 35 and 40, the bicycle loop detector symbol and the shared roadway bicycle marking, each with its area in square feet.
description:
Overall layout: Sheet 23 of the 2026 Standard Plan set, no scale. Each symbol is drawn on a labeled grid with overall dimensions and area A in square feet.

Bike lane symbol without person: Bicycle only, 3'-4" wide by 6'-0" tall, 4 in. grid, A=7 sq ft.

Bike lane symbol with person: Bicycle with a rider and helmet, 3'-4" wide by 6'-6" tall, 4 in. grid, A=7 sq ft.

International Symbol of Accessibility (ISA) marking: A blue square 4'-5" by 4'-5" containing a white outline square 3'-9" by 3'-9" and the white wheelchair symbol 2'-8 1/2" wide by 3'-0" tall, 6 in. grid. A=9 sq ft (white) and A=14 sq ft (blue). Labels show the white symbol and border and the blue field.

Diamond symbol: A diamond outline 3'-3" wide by 12'-0" long with a 6 in. wide band, 1'-0" grid, A=11 sq ft.

Numerals: Numeral 25 and numeral 35, each 4'-8" wide by 8'-0" tall on a 4 in. grid (A=17.5 sq ft for 25, A=16.5 sq ft for 35). Numeral 40, 5'-0" wide by 8'-0" tall, 4 in. grid (A=19.5 sq ft). A 1 in. dimension is shown at the left of the numeral 4.

Bicycle loop detector symbol: A bicycle with rider centered between two rectangular bars, 10 in. wide overall with the bars 2 in. wide (2 in. dimension), 1 in. grid. Vertical dimensions top to bottom: 1'-8" bar, 3", 1'-8" bicycle zone, 3", 1'-8" bar, with 5'-6" overall. The bars have zigzag break symbols. A=2 sq ft.

Shared roadway bicycle marking: Three chevrons (3'-3" wide, 6 in. spacing between bands, 2'-0" vertical dimension for the chevron group) above a bicycle without rider. The chevron group is 3'-6" tall, the bicycle 5'-9" tall, overall height 9'-3", with a 1 in. dimension at the base. 6 in. grid, A=11.5 sq ft.
notes:
1. Minor variations in dimensions may be accepted by the Engineer.

Symbol labels and colors: ISA marking shown in white and blue. Return to Table of Contents link at the bottom of the page.

title: Pavement Markings, Words
summary: Caltrans 2026 Standard Plan A24D gives dimensioned grid drawings of 18 pavement word markings with their overall widths, heights and areas, plus a table of areas and four notes on word order, word spacing and tolerances. Most words are 8 ft tall. COMPACT, BIKE and LANE are 4 ft tall.
description:
Overall layout: Sheet 24 of the 2026 Standard Plan set, no scale. Each word is drawn as outlined elongated letters on a grid (4 in. grid for 8'-0" tall words, 2 in. grid for 4'-0" tall words) with overall width, height and area A in square feet. A WORD MARKINGS table sits at the lower right of the notes.

RUNAWAY: 11'-4" wide by 8'-0" tall, A=43 sq ft.
VEHICLES: 12'-0" wide by 8'-0" tall, A=42 sq ft.
YIELD: 7'-0" wide by 8'-0" tall, A=24 sq ft.
SCHOOL: 9'-8" wide by 8'-0" tall, A=35 sq ft.
WAIT: 5'-4" wide by 8'-0" tall, A=19 sq ft.
SLOW: 6'-4" wide by 8'-0" tall, A=23 sq ft.
AHEAD: 8'-0" wide by 8'-0" tall, A=31 sq ft.
TURN: 6'-4" wide by 8'-0" tall, A=24 sq ft.
HERE: 6'-4" wide by 8'-0" tall, A=26 sq ft.
XING: 5'-4" wide by 8'-0" tall, A=21 sq ft.
SIGNAL: 8'-8" wide by 8'-0" tall, A=32 sq ft.
LEFT: 6'-4" wide by 8'-0" tall, A=19 sq ft.
RIGHT: 7'-0" wide by 8'-0" tall, A=26 sq ft.
STOP: 6'-4" wide by 8'-0" tall, A=22 sq ft.
PED: 4'-8" wide by 8'-0" tall, A=18 sq ft.
COMPACT: 5'-8" wide by 4'-0" tall, 2 in. grid, A=10 sq ft.
BIKE: 2'-8" wide by 4'-0" tall, 2 in. grid, A=5 sq ft.
LANE: 3'-2" wide by 4'-0" tall, 2 in. grid, A=6 sq ft.

Word Markings table (item and area in sq ft, two columns of pairs): RUNAWAY 43, VEHICLES 42, YIELD 24, SCHOOL 35, WAIT 19, SLOW 23, AHEAD 31, TURN 24, HERE 26, XING 21, SIGNAL 32, LEFT 19, RIGHT 26, STOP 22, PED 18, COMPACT 10, BIKE 5, LANE 6.
notes:
1. If a message consists of more than one word, it must read "UP", i.e., the first word must be nearest the driver.

2. The space between words must be at least four times the height of the characters for low speed roads, but not more than ten times the height of the characters. The space may be reduced appropriately where there is limited space because of local conditions.

3. Minor variations in dimensions may be accepted by the Engineer.

4. Portions of a letter, number or symbol may be separated by connecting segments not to exceed 2 in. in width.
